Chrysoprasus
kris-OP-ruh-sus
noun
Greek chrysoprasos (G5556) — literally "gold-leek," an apple-green to leek-green variety of chalcedony colored by trace nickel; the tenth foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20). Compound of chrysos (gold) + prason (leek).

📖 Biblical Definition

Chrysoprasus appears only at Revelation 21:20 as the tenth foundation stone of the New Jerusalem. The Greek name chrysoprasos combines chrysos (gold) and prason (leek) — "gold-leek" — describing the stone's pale yellow-green color, like a young leek shoot or apple flesh. Modern chrysoprase is a translucent variety of chalcedony (microcrystalline quartz) colored by trace nickel; it is sometimes called the "stone of Venus" in occult circles but its place in Scripture is purely as one of the twelve named foundation stones. The number ten in Scripture is the number of human completion or ordering (ten commandments; ten plagues on Egypt; ten cities of the Decapolis; the tithe). The tenth foundation, chrysoprasus, sits at the position of human-side completion — and the city's foundation is complete because God Himself has chosen and laid every stone. Three of the twelve stones share the chrysos root: chrysolite (gold-stone, the seventh), chrysoprasus (gold-leek, the tenth), and the city itself is golden (Rev 21:18, 21). The Holy Spirit has woven gold into the foundation of the city not by accident but to signal that the city is treasure — and that even its mineral catalog points to the One who is the treasure hidden in the field (Matt 13:44).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An apple-green chalcedony; the tenth foundation of the New Jerusalem.

CHRYSOPRASUS, noun. A pale apple-green or leek-green variety of chalcedony, colored by trace nickel. The Greek name means "gold-leek."

In Scripture, mentioned only at Rev 21:20 as the tenth foundation stone of the New Jerusalem. Modern spelling is also "chrysoprase."

📖 Key Scripture

Revelation 21:20 — "The ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst."

Revelation 21:18 — "And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass."

Revelation 21:21 — "And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass."

Matthew 13:44 — "Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Chrysoprasus is corrupted when modern New Age and occult practitioners assign it spiritual properties divorced from God, or when modernist commentary treats it as throwaway color variety rather than as a named, ordered, Spirit-selected stone.

expand to see more

Occult co-opting. Modern crystal-healing practitioners assign chrysoprase to the heart chakra, to "prosperity," to the "stone of Venus," and to various love-energy uses. The Bible's chrysoprasus is part of the divinely-ordered foundation of the city of God; it has no independent spiritual power. To strip the stone from its biblical context and assign it pagan symbolic functions is precisely the kind of syncretism the Bible repeatedly forbids.

Throwaway-stone reading. The other extreme is to treat chrysoprasus as just another item in a list — one more color in the rainbow of the city's foundations. But the Spirit named twelve specific stones in a specific order. The tenth stone, chrysoprasus, is the second of the three chrysos-named stones (chrysolite, chrysoprasus); it shares a root with the city's golden street and golden walls. The repeated gold theme is not random. The city of God is golden through-and-through — wall, street, foundations — because it is the treasure of which Christ said the kingdom is like.

Greek chrysoprasos (G5556) — literally "gold-leek," an apple-green chalcedony; tenth foundation of the New Jerusalem.

Greek chrysoprasos (G5556) — chrysoprasus; from chrysos (gold) + prason (leek)

Tenth foundation stone of New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20) — the only canonical appearance of the word

Modern equivalent: chrysoprase, a translucent green chalcedony colored by trace nickel; mined today in Australia and Poland

Second of three chrysos-rooted stones in the city's foundation: chrysolite (7th), chrysoprasus (10th); the city itself is golden (Rev 21:18, 21)

Usage

"The tenth foundation is chrysoprasus — "gold-leek," the pale-green chalcedony that echoes the golden city above it."

"Three gold-named stones run through the city's foundation; the city itself is gold; God has built treasure into His treasure."

"Don't buy a chrysoprase for the heart chakra; receive the heart-chakra-free Christ who is the actual treasure of the kingdom."
